text:
alice: Quick check before the follow-up — do we expose a resume token (cursor) on the public SDK iterable, or keep resume opaque and do transparent transport-level retries? Need tradeoffs across Python/TS/Go.

ben: For batch consumers I vote for explicit resume tokens. They often want to persist progress outside process restarts.

carla: Hidden resumable is nicer for the 90% case. But it leaks complexity into the transport and makes idempotency ambiguous for callers.

david: Exposing tokens forces long-term stability of token schema, which is a maintenance burden. Also surface area for security concerns if users persist tokens long-term.

alice: Streaming cases make this worse — if we stream events, do we emit a partial token mid-stream? how do you resume a stream?

ben: Proposal: two-layer API surface: a high-level ergonomic iterator that does transparent retries, plus a low-level cursor API for power users who need portability/persistence. Sketches: 

TS:
```ts
// high-level
for await (const item of client.listItems({q})) { /* simple */ }

// low-level
const start = await client.listItems.start({q});
const cursor = start.cursor;
await client.listItems.resume(cursor);
```

Python:
```py
# high-level
for item in client.list_items(q):
    ...

# low-level
cursor = client.list_items.start(q)
client.list_items.resume(cursor)
```

Go:
```go
it := client.ListItems(ctx, q)
for it.Next() { ... }
// low-level
cursor, _ := client.ListItemsStart(ctx, q)
client.ListItemsResume(ctx, cursor)
```

carla: That mirrors patterns in other infra libs. Implementation note: transport must carry an idempotency key + offset. We should standardize token as base64(JSON) with a small schema.

david: Base64 JSON is fine but mark it explicitly opaque in docs and include a semantic version field in the blob (so server/client can detect incompatible tokens).

alice: How should high-level transparent retries handle duplicates? Should we dedupe automatically or leave duplicates to the app? Server-side dedupe is ideal but we can't rely on every backed model to do it.

ben: Suggest high-level default: best-effort transparent retries with an optional `dedupe` flag (default false). For exactly-once requirements, recommend low-level resume + server-side dedupe.

carla: Also call out SDK parity. Python needs generator + async, TS needs async iterator, Go needs iterator idiom. Names should be idiomatic per language but semantics identical.

alice: Cancellation/abort semantics are important — support ctx/AbortSignal across all SDKs so callers can cancel long polls. Add that to the decision doc.

ci-bot: ci: rolling canary publish of sdk-client v0.12 to beta channel scheduled for Tue :rocket:

david: Two more practical concerns: 1) token TTL — we need to agree on expiration policy, and 2) token size. Keep tokens < 2KB.

ben: Docs point: show migration story if token schema changes. Include server-side compatibility policy in the spec.

alice: Summary for meeting notes I'm about to draft: 1) Two-layer API (high-level iterator + low-level resume API). 2) Token format: base64(JSON) with semver + opaque docs. 3) High-level transparent retries by default, optional dedupe flag. 4) Cancellation/Abort across SDKs. 5) Token TTL & size limits and migration policy. Anything else to add?

carla: Add example snippets for embedding/page sizes and recommended patterns for long-running consumers. Also add a short note on metrics (retries, resumed_count) to surface in Console.

alice: Great — I'll post a short decision doc + RFC follow-up PR after lunch. Thanks all.
